Quick notes from the infra profile we ran on the affected region (us-west-2) during the triage call:

- Regression correlates tightly with qprofile v2-int8 activation. We see increased cache misses in the KV cache and a higher incidence of fallback decoding codepaths where the kernel selector chooses a slower attention kernel at sequence lengths > 256.
- The model's quantized dequantization step appears to be adding CPU scheduling contention on the host when concurrency spikes; GPU utilization looks normal, but host-side stalls are higher.
- Error traces (attached snippet) show transient OOM and timeout entries originating from the decoding loop when request concurrency > 300.

Immediate mitigation recommendations (fast):
- Route 30% of traffic to v5.1 (baseline qprofile) to relieve hotpath pressure and confirm correlation.
- For the other 70%, enable a temporary qprofile patch that disables the new int8 decode path (we have a safe flag).
- If either measure brings p99 within SLA, schedule a rollback of v5.2 for the next maintenance window and re-run a controlled canary.

I'm preparing a short fallback-playbook.pdf with commands and runbook steps; Ben, can you apply routing?

- Provisioned two extra inference workers in the customer’s dedicated pool to relieve host-side scheduling pressure.
- Uploaded preliminary runbook and the fallback-playbook.pdf to the shared drive link: https://drive.redwood/reports/catalystx/2028-04-15/triage-notes.pdf
